item.title: Idea Validation — Finding a Painful Problem
item.description: Validate an idea, build the minimum viable product, and win your first paying customers. Lesson 1: Idea Validation — Finding a Painful Problem This lesson teaches you how to find out whether your business idea solves a problem painful enough that strangers will pay to make it go away — before you…

item.title: Business Models — How the Money Actually Flows
item.description: Lesson 2: Business Models — How the Money Actually Flows This lesson teaches you to choose a business model — the mechanism by which your business actually gets paid — and to map the money flow before you build anything. Beginners obsess over the product and treat the business model as an…

item.title: Building the Minimum Viable Product — Lean and Low-Cost
item.description: Lesson 3: Building the Minimum Viable Product — Lean and Low-Cost This lesson teaches you to build a minimum viable product (MVP): the smallest version of your offer that a real customer can pay for. The MVP is not a rough draft of your dream product — it is a deliberate test: what is the least I…

item.title: Pricing — How to Set Prices with Confidence
item.description: Lesson 4: Pricing — How to Set Prices with Confidence This lesson teaches you to set prices using math and testing instead of fear and guessing. Pricing is where beginners leave the most money on the table: they price too low from insecurity, or copy a competitor without understanding the costs…

item.title: Finding Your First Ten Customers
item.description: Lesson 5: Finding Your First Ten Customers This lesson teaches you to win your first ten customers by hand — through direct outreach, not advertising. Your first ten customers are special: they teach you what to build, give you honest feedback you can learn from, and prove the business works before…

item.title: A Simple Social Media System for a New Business
item.description: Lesson 6: A Simple Social Media System for a New Business This lesson teaches you a social media routine you can actually sustain: 30–45 minutes a day, built on content that teaches and proves rather than content that begs for attention. Social media is a slow compounder, not a lottery ticket —…

item.title: Money Basics — Costs, Break-Even, and Tracking
item.description: Lesson 7: Money Basics — Costs, Break-Even, and Tracking This lesson teaches you the money basics every founder needs: knowing your costs, calculating your break-even point, and tracking your numbers on one page. You do not need accounting software or a finance background — you need a clear-eyed…

item.title: Launch Checklist + Your 90-Day Action Plan
item.description: Lesson 8: Launch Checklist + Your 90-Day Action Plan This final lesson gets you launched: a concrete pre-launch checklist that catches the things beginners forget, and a 90-day action plan that turns this course into a working business.
